newsitem.title: USA: El Paso Elec. says transmission lines full.
newsitem.headline: El Paso Elec. says transmission lines full.

text.p: El Paso Electric Co asked the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) on Friday to clarify access to transmission lines linking the Texas-based utility to northern Mexico.

El Paso, which now supplies Mexico's national utility with 200 megawatts, is set to lose that business following recently concluded bidding for a contract to supply Comision Federal de Electricidad (CFE) for calendar 1997.
The Salt River Project (SPR) was the apparent low bidder for the new contract, but sources at the Arizona state agency said they were not aware a winner had been chosen.
El Paso is maintaining it does not have enough extra transmission capacity to carry power from Arizona and further into Mexico.
"We have a 600 megawatt (MW) line from Palo Verde (Wintersburg, Ariz.)," said El Paso spokesman Henry Quintana. "But it is already being used at capacity to supply our retail customers."
He noted that El Paso now supplies CFE mainly with locally produced power as well as transmissions from east Texas brought in on a 150 MW line.

The Texas utility is also asking FERC to clarify jurisdiction over international transmission access, Quintana said. "Does a utility have the right to send power over our interconnect into Mexico?" he added.
CFE is allowing SRP 10 days to work out transmssion details, according to El Paso.
